requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a systemd-managed service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: Baseline (cmd-7e5c877962c84bb9) confirmed no pre-existing inventory-worker service. Executor wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, ran daemon-reload and enable --now, and directly observed 'active (running)' + 'enabled' status with the correct MainPID running the exact worker binary (cmd-06fffae795934369). Post-restart recheck (cmd-26bb232cd79c4634) confirms the service is still active/enabled after a reboot, showing durable systemd management.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: Baseline showed no existing inventorysvc user (cmd-7e5c877962c84bb9). Executor created it as a system account (useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin) and the unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc. Process listing directly shows PID 2802 (and post-restart PID 916) running as user 'invento+' (truncated inventorysvc), confirming the worker process actually runs under that account rather than just being configured to (cmd-06fffae795934369, cmd-26bb232cd79c4634).

requirements.requirement: The managed service executes the specified binary /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1
requirements.summary: ExecStart is set to the exact path, and the ps output for the MainPID directly shows '/bin/sh /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker' both before and after the restart, matching the pre-existing binary confirmed in the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 83a0a80f... with service active/enabled was captured (cmd-6a4fad17e9ba47c6), matching the fixed after-prepare boot-identity snapshot. A backgrounded systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged before the exec stream closed (cmd-8ee237c44093493c), followed by two timed-out connectivity polls consistent with the node being down (cmd-432a6d62656a46dd, cmd-8ca58092128e4047), then a new boot_id 93e2b701... was observed (cmd-20799c9d9c0444c9), matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot exactly. Post-restart, the service was confirmed active/enabled with the correct user/process (cmd-26bb232cd79c4634), demonstrating full recovery through systemd persistence.

overall_summary: The task was fully satisfied: os-comparison-worker is running on node1 as the systemd service inventory-worker under the dedicated inventorysvc system account, verified by direct process/user inspection both before and after a reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with high-quality, internally consistent evidence (boot-identity change matches the fixed lifecycle snapshots exactly) and full recovery of the service after the restart.
limitations: Connectivity-timeout evidence during the reboot window (cmd-432a6d62656a46dd, cmd-8ca58092128e4047) shows the node was unreachable but does not itself prove a full shutdown/boot cycle beyond the boot_id change; this is standard for exec-based restart verification and is corroborated by the fixed snapshot cross-check.

No functional/data output from the worker itself was captured (it is a simple sleep-loop placeholder binary per its script contents), so 'data state' recovery was inferred from process and service status only, which is appropriate given the binary's trivial nature.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task or restart-protocol purposes: user creation and unit file/enable (cmd-06fffae795934369) implement the required outcome, and the reboot (cmd-8ee237c44093493c) is the mandatory restart-evidence action. No troubleshooting experiments, failed services, or damaged package state appear in either snapshot (failed-services and package-health are identical before/after). One minor, low-risk residue: /tmp/reboot.log, created by redirecting the backgrounded reboot command's output, remains in the after-executor temp-files snapshot and was not cleaned up; this is bounded, non-sensitive, and a byproduct of an authorized action rather than an unnecessary mutation, so it only lightly reduces the hygiene score.
